messages.content: I am ready to settle the New York flights. Compare the real total for all three of us, including one checked bag each, and account for airport cars and how much of Friday and Wednesday the different schedules consume.

The fares have repriced. The LaGuardia pair is still available: Friday DFW-LGA 6:45-11:04 p.m. and Wednesday LGA-DFW 3:40-6:43 p.m. Base airfare is $1,647 for three. One checked bag per traveler each way adds $240, and estimated private-car transfers total $150, bringing the practical total to $2,037. Friday door-to-door is roughly 5:00 p.m. to 12:15 a.m.; Wednesday you would leave a Midtown hotel around 12:45 p.m.
And the alternatives through JFK and Newark? I do not want a cheaper fare that turns into an ordeal.

The JFK outbound leaves DFW at 7:30 p.m. and arrives at 11:58 p.m. Paired with the Wednesday Newark return at 4:55 p.m., arriving DFW at 8:05 p.m., airfare is $1,518. Bags add $270 because that fare charges $45 each way, and the two airport cars are estimated at $235. Total: $2,023. You would reach the hotel around 1:30 a.m. Friday night and leave it near 1:00 p.m. Wednesday. It saves only $14 versus LaGuardia and adds a much later arrival plus a cross-river trip to Newark.
Was there also a JFK round trip, or did that disappear?

It is still there. The same 7:30 p.m. outbound pairs with a 1:25 p.m. Wednesday JFK departure, landing at DFW at 4:38 p.m. Airfare is $1,476, bags are $270, and cars are about $220, for $1,966 total. The drawback is the return: for a 1:25 p.m. flight, I would plan to leave Midtown by 9:30 a.m. It effectively gives up Wednesday morning.
Give me the ticket rules side by side. Also, is the LaGuardia price still for the cabin we discussed, not basic economy?

Correct. LaGuardia is standard main cabin: nonrefundable, changes allowed without a separate change fee, but any fare increase applies; cancellation before departure produces airline credit for each named passenger. Seats can be selected now. The JFK-Newark combination is also nonrefundable, but the outbound is basic economy: no voluntary changes and only limited cancellation credit after a $99-per-person deduction. The JFK round trip has that same basic-economy restriction in both directions, and seat assignments cost extra or may be deferred.
Then LaGuardia is clearly the workable one. Before you buy it, confirm the complete charge today and tell me what seats are actually open.

The ticket charge today is $1,647 total, including taxes, for all three passengers. Checked bags are not prepaid; assuming all three check one bag each way, $240 would be paid at check-in. Available contiguous seats include rows 21 and 24 outbound and rows 18 and 23 return. Each has a three-seat block open, with window, middle, and aisle together at no added charge.
Book it. Put me in a window seat, and seat my spouse and daughter beside me in the same row both ways.

I have the passenger names and payment method from the trip file. The purchase will charge $1,647 now. I will assign you the window, with your spouse in the middle and your daughter on the aisle, keeping all three together on both flights. Shall I submit it?

The flights are ticketed under confirmation NYC8R4: Friday, February 13, DFW-LGA 6:45-11:04 p.m., and Wednesday, February 18, LGA-DFW 3:40-6:43 p.m. The card on file was charged $1,647. Seats are 21A, 21B, and 21C outbound and 18F, 18E, and 18D return, with your seat at the window both ways. The tickets are nonrefundable and may be changed without a change fee, subject to fare difference; cancellation before departure yields passenger-specific airline credits. Checked bags remain $40 per bag each way. With six bag charges and the $150 car allowance, the projected flight-and-transfer total is $2,037. The LaGuardia timing now supports a late Friday hotel arrival around midnight and a Wednesday hotel departure around 12:45 p.m.; the two hotel candidates remain unreserved pending their room and cancellation checks.
